pages.text: The Advanced Potion Brewer is an automated version of the vanilla brewing stand. It uses the current $(thing)PotionBrewing$() registry directly for bottle inputs, brewing ingredients, and potion conversions, so brewing recipes added by other mods can be detected automatically.$(br2)$(bold)Role$()$(br2)$(li)Designed for batch brewing multi-step potions.$(li)Can automatically fill glass bottles with water.$(li)Can consume Time Fluid to brew faster, falling back to vanilla speed when Time Fluid is missing.$(li)Supports auto input/output, with products extracted only from the three output slots.$(br2)$(bold)Layout$()$(br2)$(bold)Item Slots$()

$(li)Bottle input slots: 3 slots, each capped to 1 glass bottle or potion.$(li)Ingredient slots: 6 slots, representing brewing steps 1-6 in order.$(li)Blaze powder slot: 1 slot, accepts blaze powder only.$(li)Product output slots: 3 slots, each capped to 1 final potion.$(br2)Ingredient order:$(br2)1. The vanilla-style ingredient slot is step 1.$(br)2. The 5 top horizontal ingredient slots are steps 2-6 from left to right.$(br2)$(bold)Fluid Tanks$()$(br2)$(li)Left water tank: accepts water.$(li)Right Time Fluid tank: accepts JDT Time Fluid.$(br2)The water tank can automatically fill glass bottles in the bottle input slots into water bottles, consuming 250 mB water per bottle.

$(bold)Controls$()$(br2)$(li)Speed button: sets the tick duration for each ingredient step.$(li)Redstone button: controls whether the machine obeys redstone.$(li)Input lock button: locks the current non-empty ingredient slots to their captured items.$(li)Auto I/O button: configures which world directions the machine uses for automatic input/output.$(br2)$(bold)Brewing Flow$()

1. Place glass bottles or potions in the three bottle input slots.$(br)2. Place blaze powder in the blaze powder slot.$(br)3. Place ingredients in order across ingredient steps 1-6.$(br)4. The machine checks ingredients starting from step 1.$(br)5. Empty ingredient slots are skipped; ingredients that do not apply to the current potion are skipped.$(br)6. Valid ingredients continue transforming the intermediate potions in the bottle slots.$(br)7. After all usable ingredients have been checked, final potions move to the three output slots on the right.$(br2)$(bold)Input Lock$()$(br2)Input lock records the items currently present in non-empty ingredient slots. While locked:

$(li)Captured ingredient slots only accept their captured item.$(li)Empty locked ingredient slots show a dim ghost item.$(li)Hovering a locked ingredient slot shows the locked item name.$(li)Bottle slots, output slots, and the blaze powder slot are not locked.$(br2)This is useful for fixed brewing chains, such as "water bottle -> awkward potion -> upgraded potion -> extended potion".$(br2)$(bold)Automation$()$(br2)$(bold)Item Automation$()

$(li)Auto input recognizes bottle slots, the blaze powder slot, and ingredient slots.$(li)Blaze powder is inserted into the blaze powder slot before ingredient slots.$(li)Auto output extracts only from the three product output slots. It will not extract bottles, ingredients, or blaze powder.$(br2)$(bold)Fluid Automation$()$(br2)$(li)The water tank can receive water automatically.$(li)The Time Fluid tank can receive Time Fluid automatically.$(li)Both tanks also support right-click fluid container transfer.$(br2)$(bold)Speed And Time Fluid$()$(br2)$(bold)Vanilla Speed Relation$()

A vanilla brewing stand takes 400 ticks per ingredient step. The Advanced Potion Brewer speed button is the tick duration for each ingredient step:$(br2)$(li)$(thing)1$(): fastest setting.$(li)$(thing)400$(): vanilla speed.$(li)Above $(thing)400$(): treated as vanilla speed.$(br2)Time Fluid is charged only for ticks saved relative to vanilla speed. Without enough Time Fluid, the machine falls back to vanilla 400-tick speed.$(br2)$(bold)Cost Derivation$()$(br2)The cost is derived from a JDT Time Wand accelerating a vanilla brewing stand:

$(li)A 256x JDT Time Wand effect lasts 600 ticks.$(li)256x adds 256 extra block-entity ticks per tick.$(li)Total extra ticks: 600 × 256 = 153,600.$(li)One vanilla brewing step takes 400 ticks.$(li)153,600 extra ticks are equivalent to 384 full brewing steps.$(br2)Other Time Wand rates have the same efficiency:

$(bold)Time Wand rate | Extra ticks in 30 seconds | Theoretical full brewing steps | Time Fluid cost$()$(br)2x | 1,200 | 3 | 2 × JDT Time Wand fluid cost$(br)4x | 2,400 | 6 | 4 × JDT Time Wand fluid cost$(br)8x | 4,800 | 12 | 8 × JDT Time Wand fluid cost$(br)16x | 9,600 | 24 | 16 × JDT Time Wand fluid cost$(br)32x | 19,200 | 48 | 32 × JDT Time Wand fluid cost$(br)64x | 38,400 | 96 | 64 × JDT Time Wand fluid cost$(br)128x | 76,800 | 192 | 128 × JDT Time Wand fluid cost$(br)256x | 153,600 | 384 | 256 × JDT Time Wand fluid cost$(br2)Therefore each full 400-tick brewing step costs:$(br2)$(thing)JDT Time Wand fluid cost × 2 ÷ 3$()

The machine then charges only for ticks saved by the current speed:$(br2)$(thing)cost = full 400-tick cost × saved ticks ÷ 400$()$(br2)At $(thing)1 tick$(), it charges the full saved-step cost, equivalent to:$(br2)$(thing)256 × JDT Time Wand fluid cost ÷ 384$()$(br2)$(bold)Upgrade Effects$()$(br2)$(bold)Upgrade | Effect$()$(br)Creative | Removes FE and Time Fluid cost$(br)Capacity | Increases FE and fluid capacity$(br)Fluid | Increases fluid capacity only$(br2)$(bold)Crafting$()
